section_summary: This section moves from an appeal for a conciliatory peace with Japan to reports on Japanese politicians, local politics in Kyushu, and reactions to a future Japanese peace settlement. Its largest documents are a field study of rural and industrial politics in Kyushu and the opening of a historical report on Japanese proletarian movements.

subfiles.title: Appeal concerning a just peace and the renunciation of war
subfiles.to: American people through George Atcheson Jr.
subfiles.about: Hashimoto urges the victors to consult defeated nations and pursue lasting peace without punitive discrimination.
subfiles.summary: The concluding pages argue that a unilateral treaty, economic restrictions and punishment without repentance could breed resentment and another war. Hashimoto praises U.S. leadership while asking that the principle of renouncing war be considered by all nations.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting Hashimoto's views on Japan
subfiles.about: Hashimoto offers his memorandum on democracy in Japan and Japanese-American friendship.
subfiles.summary: Hashimoto asks Atcheson to read his views on Japan's future.

subfiles.title: Police information on Tetsuma Hashimoto and the Shiunso Society
subfiles.from: Not stated; based on information from Tsuneichi Kawajiri
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: A police account describes Hashimoto's career, the Shiunso Society and his prewar advocacy of Japanese-American friendship.
subfiles.summary: The account traces Hashimoto's political work and the Shiunso Society's support for the emperor system, pacifism, anti-communism and pro-Americanism. It reports that postwar investigators found no fault with the society.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement form for despatch 1100
subfiles.about: A copy of Tokyo despatch 1100 is designated to replace an unreturned original.
subfiles.summary: Directs return of the replacement record copy for filing.

subfiles.title: Current political situation and personalities: conversation with Saburō Kurusu
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards a conversation with Kurusu about Yoshida, Liberal Party opposition and personnel changes.
subfiles.summary: It summarizes Kurusu's expectation that Yoshida will assume active Liberal Party leadership and eventually return to office. It also notes Liberal views of Foreign Minister Ashida and expected Central Liaison Office changes.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation with Saburō Kurusu
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Kurusu explains Liberal Party coalition tactics, Yoshida's prospects and Liberal attitudes toward Ashida.
subfiles.summary: Kurusu says Yoshida kept the Liberals out of the coalition because of Socialist leftists, despite pressure from party members seeking cabinet posts. He expects Yoshida to consolidate the party after Hatoyama's purge and predicts Ashida will replace some Central Liaison Office personnel.

subfiles.title: File note on Kyushu field-trip memorandum
subfiles.about: A reviewer briefly comments on the forthcoming three-week Kyushu field-trip report.
subfiles.summary: Calls the report fairly interesting and notes selected passages.

subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding local politics in Japan
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards McLean's study of politics in three Kyushu communities.
subfiles.summary: Introduces a study contrasting conservative farm and fishing communities with an industrial city.

subfiles.title: Local Politics in Kyushu
subfiles.from: John A. McLean, Political Affairs Division
subfiles.about: McLean analyzes local government, economic conditions and election behavior in Sue, Hirado and Iizuka.
subfiles.summary: The report describes village government, agricultural and fishing associations, cooperatives, land reform and labor unions. It finds prosperous farmers and fishermen generally conservative, while industrial Iizuka gives stronger support to Social Democrats. McLean argues that personal reputation, local consultation, group loyalty and entrenched officials still shape elections, although democratic reforms are gaining ground. Weak transport and limited access to newspapers and radio slow political change.

subfiles.title: Mukden press comment on Japan and regional government
subfiles.about: The telegram summarizes Chinese newspaper editorials on Japan's peace terms, trade and northeastern government reform.
subfiles.summary: Reports editorials warning against lenient terms for Japan and questioning trade with it.

subfiles.summary: Cover of the Civil Intelligence Section's special report.

subfiles.title: Transmission of report on Japanese proletarian politics
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards five copies of a historical report on Japanese proletarian movements.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the Civil Intelligence Section report and describes its scope.

subfiles.title: Left Wing–Right Wing: Japanese Proletarian Politics
subfiles.from: Civil Intelligence Section, Far East Command
subfiles.about: The report surveys Japanese proletarian parties and unions, then begins a history of socialism from 1882 through the early twentieth century.
subfiles.summary: The title, contents, sources and preamble outline a historical account of Japanese proletarian politics and a reference section on parties and unions. The opening chapter follows early socialist organizations, the split between parliamentary and direct-action factions, the Red Flag Incident and the High Treason Case; it includes a table of defendants and sentences. The first page of Chapter II turns to the growth of democratic and proletarian ideas after the First World War and clashes between liberal writers and nationalist societies.
